subject: MedSync bake-off: prioritized decision criteria & POC next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Alvarez <elena@medsynchealth.com>, Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MedSync bake-off: prioritized decision criteria & POC next steps

Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed POC plan so we can align on scope and timeline. I pulled together the attached scope and the RFP answers you requested (attached).

Key pain points you called out:
- Slow transcription and annotation latency for real-time scribe workflows (spikes at 800–1,200 tokens/sec per session).
- Cost variability when traffic bursts hit (30–40% monthly overage last quarter).
- Data residency and strict audit logging for PHI-related requests.

Primary goals for the POC:
1) Match current latency at 95th percentile for 30 concurrent scribe sessions (target: <220ms per token).
2) Demonstrate predictable unit cost under burst load (target: <20% variance at 2x baseline).
3) Verify audit logs and KMS integration meet your compliance checklist.

Decision criteria (ranked):
1) Latency & throughput behavior under burst (weight: 35%)
2) Data/security posture & auditability (25%)
3) Cost predictability (20%)
4) Operational simplicity / rollout risk (10%)
5) Feature parity for streaming and function-calling (10%)

Proposed POC tests (short list):
- Baseline latency: 30 concurrent streaming sessions, human-like prompt mix (we run this with your sample prompts).
- Burst resilience: synthetic ramp to 2–3x concurrent sessions for 1–2 minutes to observe queuing/batch effects.
- Cold-start cache impact: measure first-token penalty and KV cache warm-up time.
- Auditability: generate and review token-level log entries for a sample of PHI-containing requests.

Competitive snapshot (we discussed two vendors on the call):
- BeaconAI: lower per-token list price but heavier queuing at bursts observed in public benchmarks.
- NimbusServe: strong on throughput but requires significant infra configuration and lacks turnkey audit-log exports.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the top-3 decision criteria and any must-have compliance items (by Wed 7/21).
- We schedule a 2-hour POC kickoff week of 7/26 with engineering and security (I can send invites).
- Redwood will provide a POC env, a test harness (scripts), and a short runbook for your team.

Attachments: MedSync-POC-scope.xlsx (POC tasks & acceptance criteria), MedSync-RFP-answers.pdf (responses to your spreadsheet).

If that all sounds right, I'll draft the mutual action plan and invite the engineers.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0139
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Alvarez <elena@medsynchealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@medsynchealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSync bake-off: prioritized decision criteria & POC next steps

Thanks, Kimberly — good recap. A few clarifications from our side (procurement and security are looped in separately):

On criteria: we agree with your ranking but swap cost predictability and data/security to make security #2 — PHI handling and auditability are non-negotiable for our procurement team.

Must-have compliance items:
- End-to-end encryption for logs in transit and at rest.
- Ability to export audit logs daily to our S3 bucket.
- KMS integration with our Azure Key Vault.

Timeline constraints:
- We need a vendor decision by 8/16 to meet the product roadmap.
- Procurement expects a template SOW and an estimate for a 3-month POC (heads-down) by 7/30.

Questions for your team before the kickoff:
1) Can Redwood push logs to our S3 export endpoint or do we need to pull?
2) Do you offer a non-prod VPC-based deployment for the POC?

We can confirm top-priority criteria by EOD Wed (7/21).

—Elena
Elena Alvarez
VP Product, MedSync Health
elena@medsynchealth.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Alvarez <elena@medsynchealth.com>, Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSync bake-off: prioritized decision criteria & POC next steps

Appreciate the clarification, Elena — we will treat security as #2 and make those compliance items explicit in the SOW. Quick answers to the questions and some competitive notes for your evaluation team: 

Answers:
- Logs: Redwood can push daily audit log exports to your S3 endpoint; we also keep a retained copy in the customer console for 30 days. We support S3 push and can ship to an S3-compatible endpoint if you prefer.
- Non-prod VPC: Yes — we can provide a Private POC deployment inside a VPC with customer-managed networking and KMS integration (we'll need an SSH jump host & egress rules).

Competitive considerations to include in your matrix:
- BeaconAI typically relies on multi-tenant endpoints which can be cheaper but limits log export granularity and makes KMS integration more complex.
- NimbusServe gives strong throughput but we've seen customers do more engineering work to reach predictable unit cost under burst; Redwood's autoscaling + prefix/KV caching reduces per-token cost variance without manual tuning.

POC estimate ask for procurement: we'll prepare a 3-month POC estimate (engineering hours + reserved capacity for tests) and share a template SOW by 7/30. I'll include cost bands for the two capacity profiles we discussed (standard reserved pool vs dedicated burst buffer).

Suggested concrete POC tests (expanded):
1) Stream latency suite (30 sessions) — 3 runs at different times of day.
2) Burst stress (2x, 3x ramps) — measure tail latency and queue depth.
3) Billing simulation: replay a week's production mix to estimate variance.
4) Audit verification: generate 100 sample PHI requests and show S3 export + KMS-wrapped logs.

Open items for kickoff prep:
- Engineering contact at MedSync for VPC networking (ext firewall rules and jump host).
- Sample prompt corpus + production token mix CSV.
- Procurement email for SOW / billing contact.

I'll schedule the kickoff for the week of 7/26 and attach the draft SOW once Marissa and I review it internally.

Thanks —
Kimberly
From: Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@medsynchealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Elena Alvarez <elena@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSync bake-off: prioritized decision criteria & POC next steps

Kimberly / Elena — this is all helpful. A couple quick items from my side before procurement fully engages: 

1) SLA & fallback: what are Redwood's SLA targets for dedicated POC capacity and do you offer an automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted tier if the dedicated pool saturates? We need to understand failure modes.
2) Ballpark cost: can you provide a rough monthly cost range for the two capacity profiles you mentioned? Procurement doesn't need exacts yet, just a range for budgeting.

If you can include these in the SOW draft that would be great. Also confirm that the POC can be scoped so that any production keys/data remain in our account (we prefer you to deploy into our non-prod subscription).

We'll confirm the priority criteria EOD today. Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Tom
